about: Models the maintainers declare good enough to take a game to Silver without a proven game or a check (AGENTS.md, "Model"). Exact ids, as a session names them; a context-window suffix such as [1m] is ignored when ids are compared, so it needs no entry of its own. A model that took a game to Silver before the maintainer's check existed needs no entry here: kit/scripts/models.py finds those in the records. A game that passed a maintainer's check proves no model, so declare one here when its samples earn it (kit/CHECKING.md). A line of models is declared under `lines`: every model of the line at or above the version in `from` is proven, whatever version follows it, so a new model of the line needs no entry. kit/scripts/models.py says how an id is read as a line and a version.

claude-opus.why: Claude Opus from 5.5 on, declared good enough by the maintainers on 11 November 2026: Opus 5.5 is the lowest proven model of its line, and every later one counts as proven

claude-fable.why: Claude Fable from 5.1 on, declared good enough by the maintainers on 11 November 2026: Fable 5.1 is the lowest proven model of its line, and every later one counts as proven
